VERSION.value: netlib.org/quadpack as served 2026-09-12 (per-file; no tarball endpoint)

value.lineage: quadpack (netlib historical distribution): the authoritative Fortran source as served by netlib.org, the authors' own channel

value.built_to: numerically integrate a function of one variable, ADAPTING the subdivision to the estimated error (Gauss-Kronrod rules + epsilon extrapolation), including singular and infinite ranges
value.pressure: an integrand whose difficulty varies across the interval; fixed rules waste effort or miss features, so the routine spends evaluations where the estimated error is largest
value.success_means: the returned integral is within the requested absolute/relative tolerance, with a returned error estimate; QUADPACK's own test battery

ANCESTRY.value: quadpack (netlib historical distribution): the authoritative Fortran source as served by netlib.org, the authors' own channel

cut.note: adaptive quadrature as three mechanisms: a Gauss-Kronrod pair (21 points) that returns an estimate and an error estimate from the difference of its two rules; globally adaptive bisection that always splits the subinterval with the largest error estimate (a sorted list maintained by dqpsrt) until the total error meets the tolerance or the subdivision limit; and Wynn's epsilon algorithm applied to the sequence of partial results to extrapolate through end-point singularities, with round-off detection that switches extrapolation off

organs.human_name: dqk21 (called at 240, 289-290; body not read); result, abserr, resabs, resasc
organs.mechanism: a 21-point Kronrod rule shares its nodes with an embedded 10-point Gauss rule; the two estimates' difference, scaled by the integral of |f - mean| (resasc) with a heuristic power, gives the error estimate; both the value and the error come from one set of 21 function evaluations
assumptions: the Kronrod extension of a Gauss rule is the cheapest way to get an error estimate from the same points (Kronrod 1965)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one function evaluation set per interval yields value and error
organs.human_prior: Kronrod 1965; Piessens' scaling of the error
organs.source_boundary: dqk21; CANDIDATE because the body was not read

organs.human_name: dqagse.f 250-390: the main loop; dqpsrt (346) maintains the descending order of error estimates; limit; the two-interval error sum; ier codes 1-5 (limit, roundoff, bad integrand behaviour, divergence, invalid input)
organs.mechanism: the interval is split at the midpoint of whichever subinterval currently has the largest error estimate; the two halves are integrated by the rule; the list of subintervals is kept sorted by error estimate (a partial insertion sort that only moves the new entries); the loop stops when the sum of error estimates is within the absolute or relative tolerance, when the subdivision limit is reached, or when round-off is detected (the error estimate stops decreasing as intervals shrink)
organs.output: the integral, the error, an ier code
organs.state: the interval lists (alist, blist, rlist, elist, iord)
assumptions: error is concentrated where the integrand is hard, so refining the worst interval is the best use of evaluations
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a smooth integrand with an undetected feature between rule points can pass (ier 0) with a wrong answer; the ier codes are the documented failure landscape

organs.human_name: dqelg (called at 384; header read): the condensed epsilon table; numrl2, rlist2, res3la; ier 2 'roundoff error is detected in the extrapolation table'; the 'extrapolation' flag path in dqagse
organs.mechanism: as bisection concentrates on a singular end point, the partial sums over the shrinking intervals form a sequence converging slowly; Wynn's epsilon algorithm (a nonlinear sequence transformation equivalent to Shanks / Pade) is applied to the sequence to estimate its limit and an error; the extrapolated result replaces the plain sum when its error is smaller; the table is limited (limexp) and the routine detects when round-off dominates and stops extrapolating
organs.state: the epsilon table and the last three results
assumptions: algebraic-logarithmic end-point singularities produce sequences the epsilon algorithm accelerates (de Doncker's analysis)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: integrands with end-point singularities converge in far fewer evaluations; the reason qags is the default in scipy
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: extrapolation can be fooled by non-singular slow convergence; the round-off detector is the guard

rejected_cuts.candidate: the other rules (qk15/31/41/51/61), the weight-function integrators (qawo, qaws, qawc, qawf), qagi (infinite range by transformation), qagp (user-given singular points), qng (non-adaptive), the single-precision twins

rejected_cuts.evidence: the rule, the adaptive strategy and the extrapolation are separable and separately published

pressures.condition: an organism integrates a black-box f over [a, b]; some integrands are smooth, some have algebraic or logarithmic end-point singularities, some are pathological; the score is evaluations to reach the tolerance and the honesty of the reported error
pressures.failure_condition: a wrong answer reported as converged, or evaluations growing without bound on a singular integrand
pressures.world_punishes: uniform refinement; no error estimate; no extrapolation
pressures.world_rewards: embedded error estimates, worst-first bisection, sequence extrapolation with round-off detection
pressures.observable_consequence: evaluations and true error vs reported error on the Piessens test set with extrapolation on and off
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: an integrand-specific change of variables (which the world withholds)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the analytic integral must report zero error; bisection without extrapolation must need orders of magnitude more evaluations on x^-0.5-type integrands; the pathological integrand must return ier != 0 rather than a confident wrong answer: the world must show all three

ancestry_edges.to: Kronrod 1965; Wynn 1956; Piessens et al. 1983; the netlib mirror is the authors' channel (record)

unexplained: rule bodies and the special-purpose integrators unread
residue.note: the three mechanisms of the default integrator are located; the rule itself is CANDIDATE
